test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 26 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A dealer incurs a loss of 5% if he sells an article for ₹1805. At what price must he sell the article so as to gain 5% on that article?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the unitary method, we can find the new selling price directly from the ratio of percentages.

Given SP₁ corresponds to a 5% loss (95% of CP).

Target SP₂ corresponds to a 5% gain (105% of CP).

Target SP₂ = SP₁ × (105 ÷ 95)

Target SP₂ = 1805 × (21 ÷ 19) = 95 × 21 = 1995

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1995.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹1805

Loss percentage = 5%

Target Profit percentage = 5%

 
 CP (100%)
 ₹1900
 
 
 SP₁ (95%)
 ₹1805
 
 
 SP₂ (105%)
 ₹?
 
 

 

 −5%
 
 

 

 +5%

 Profit & Loss Flow

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP × [100 ÷ (100 − Loss%)]

New Selling Price (SP₂) = CP × [(100 + Profit%) ÷ 100]

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = 1805 × [100 ÷ (100 − 5)]

⇒ CP = 1805 × (100 ÷ 95)

⇒ CP = 19 × 100 = ₹1900

⇒ To gain 5%, SP₂ = 1900 × [(100 + 5) ÷ 100]

⇒ SP₂ = 1900 × (105 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP₂ = 19 × 105 = 1995

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1995.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP)

CP is considered as the base value (100%). All standard profit and loss calculations are measured against the CP.

Marked Price (MP)

MP is the catalog price. Discounts are always evaluated on the Marked Price: SP = MP × [(100 − Discount%) ÷ 100].

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer uses a false weight, Profit% = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.
